pf.money.before: Nothing taken to book any meeting or the first call. No card saved, no hold, no deposit at booking.

pf.money.never: Rosie never takes an assignment of an insurance policy, and never sells or holds planning-ahead money. Preneed contracts and their trust funds stay with the home.
pf.money.fees: No missed-meeting or late-cancel fee: meetings are free to move or cancel.
pf.money.outside costs: Items the home pays others for, like death certificates or a cemetery's fee, show on the statement as the home's own lines, as the state's rules require.
pf.money.tax: Only where the state's rules tax an item, from the state form.
pf.money.deposit cap: Any limit on deposits comes from the state form.
pf.money.rosfield: The funeral home pays Rosfield's $2 per confirmed booking: an arrangement meeting, a planning-ahead meeting, or a first call sent through Rosie. notes:
From the lawyer pilot (pattern consult). Why: a funeral home is like a law office at a hard moment. A licensed, named person (the director) meets the family, the first meeting is set by the AI, and private details go only on the secure page. The lawyer's grief-free, named-only shape fit better than a clinic or a home service.
Cast: Sam Lee owns two companies. Lee Memorial Chapel (flow A, 88 Linden St; cremation and memorial services; directors Helen Chen and Victor Diaz) takes the master's second-company place. Lee Funeral Home (flow B, 1200 Cedar Ave; funeral care, plus planning ahead as its second kind of work; directors Henry Price and Clara Moore) takes the main company's place. Sam is a licensed director too. Pat stays the office manager. Alex M. is the family member in both flows; Alex has no set pronoun.
License numbers are fake on purpose (EX-FD-1042 Sam, EX-FD-3155 Henry, EX-PN-4180 Helen's preneed seller license, EX-PN-3041 Henry's, EX-FE-2077 and EX-FE-3105 the establishments). Which licenses a state needs is a switch from the state's form (plugin pf.license); nothing names one state or city.
Money paths, flow A: visit|none|bill (main: a free arrangement meeting, the services chosen and priced there, a deposit's bill at DONE when the family signs, the rest's bill before the service day); visit|none|counter (the chapel's own way: its card reader, a check, or an insurance policy it handles in its own tools); list|none|counter (a free planning-ahead meeting from the price list, nothing paid through Rosie).
Money paths, flow B: visit|none|bill (main, same as A); visit|none|own (the home's own way, including an insurance policy); list|none|own (a free planning-ahead meeting). The master's sign-up example was not a reason to list a path.
Rosie never takes an assignment of an insurance policy, never handles a preneed contract or trust money, and never touches case files, death certificates, permits, obituaries or cemetery and crematory paperwork. The home does all of that in its own tools (plugin pf.money, pf.rules; A9-03, B9-17).
Price list first: A8-23 and B8-18 give the general price list to keep before any talk of choices, and the time it was given is saved. The family chooses only what it wants (A8-25). Prices by phone: own branch A3-x01 and B3-x01 (on a call) and A7-x01 (by text before the meeting), read word for word from the price list. Rosie never says what the law requires (like embalming); it quotes the price list.
Who may decide: own steps A8-x01 and A8-x02 (B8-x01, B8-x02) before the statement. Who has the right is a switch from the state's form (plugin pf.rules). If someone who shares the right wants to wait, nothing is final or billed and the home follows up itself.
The service date: own step A8-x03 and B8-x03 set it with the outside places (cemetery, crematory, place of worship), each confirmed by the home. A10-x01 and A10-x02 (B10-x01, B10-x02) send a page the family forwards, and one gentle note the day before. That date never moves and is never offered 'a new time': if the director can't come, the home names another director.
First call (bringing the person into care from home, hospice or a care home, any hour): flow B's sent-now branch (B4-81, B4-19, B6-16 to B6-18, B7-48 to B7-50, B8-58), with the director on call reached right away. In flow A the hospice house calls the chapel's line itself (A4-43). The first call counts its own $2; the arrangement meeting the next morning is its own booking.
Safety: an unexpected death at home, or a death not under hospice, gets 911 first, and nobody moves the person until the authorities say so (A3-24, B3-19). Under hospice at home, the hospice nurse is called first (A3-23, B3-18). Crisis words keep the master's 988 and 911 (A3-25).
Nobody moves on silence: where the master moves a booking to a stand-in when the customer doesn't answer, the overlay has Sam call instead (A7-61, B7-22, S11-46, S11-49).
Grief first: the rating is off (A10-34 takes 'No: never after a death'; B10-02 is off because B has no switch, see the gap). No tips (A9-07), no 'book again', no proposals, no sales texts after a death, no storage fee on ashes (A10-30, B10-27 off: one gentle text, then the director calls). Waitlist off in B. The no-show text is gentle and asks no fee.
Private details (cause of death, medical details, the Social Security number, family money) go only on the secure page, never in a text, including owner and staff texts. The reminder asks for papers only if the family has them.
Timelines, flow A: Alex asks Fri Oct 23 8:15am; the meeting is Sat Oct 24 11:00am with Helen; DONE 1:05pm with a $2,585 statement ($1,000 deposit today, $1,585 billed Tue Oct 27, due Wed Oct 28); the memorial service is Thu Oct 29 11:00am at St. Mark's Church; the ashes are READY before it.
